avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional lots. Boroughs add their own resources: parks fund money, equipment rentals, blue-collar worker teams. Exemptions also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expenditure is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for parks purposes to the purchase of trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including plant planting, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report no later than December 31, 2026, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Spring cleaning of streets and sidewalks
etapes.texte: Several boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives after winter. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expenditure of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four vacuum sweepers and three tanker trucks in 2026 and 2027.

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is entrusting companies with the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

Montréal-Nord is paying for an additional rented grader during the 2025-2026 winter and Saint-Léonard is allocating $200,000 in surplus to its 2026 snow removal operations, after 39 abrasive spreadings since November 15, 2025, while the budget had planned for 20. The City and some boroughs are extending turnkey snow removal, towing and equipment rental with operators contracts by 12 months.

etapes.titre: Snow removal at parks and buildings
etapes.texte: The City is extending snow removal for the parking lot of the édifice Jacinthe-Fyfe and for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the stade de soccer de Montréal. It is also awarding a contract for snow removal of service roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal services for the Grand parc de l'Ouest cover two seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031, with each season running from November 1 to April 15.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its drinking water and sewer networks, in several boroughs and on main pipes. It is also continuing the wastewater disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte treatment plant and paying for the day-to-day operation of this plant. Boroughs are taking charge of replacing lead water service lines, including the portion located on private land.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining them, without digging a trench, and to redo the pavement on various streets in many boroughs. These contracts include replacing lead water service connections on both the public side and the private side.

etapes.titre: Lead water service lines on private land
etapes.texte: Boroughs are offering city council the option of taking charge of replacing lead service lines located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the property owners concerned [CA26 22 0034].

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild water pipes and infrastructure along rue Guy and on rue De Champlain, and is adding funds to the contracts for rue Saint-Antoine Ouest and rue de la Cathédrale. On rue De Champlain, the project will replace a 1,200 mm pipe installed in 1927 [CG26 0332].

The City is renewing or awarding contracts to operate the treatment plant: process control system, chemical products, residue burial, housekeeping, upgrading of sludge incinerators and mechanical work. The mechanical work is aimed in particular at reconditioning bar screens damaged during heavy rainfall [CG26 0543].

aSurveiller.texte: Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026, then incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Adoption planned for October 19, 2026 of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
Rehabilitation work on the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord to be completed by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
Completion of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Rue Guy project planned until December 2027; the ozone plant is expected to come into service in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrade.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward several projects at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. It is launching construction of a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, replacing electrical equipment at the site, renewing park maintenance, and redeveloping rue De Louvain nearby. It is also asking the Québec government for money for a cycling and pedestrian link.

etapes.texte: The City is requesting financial assistance from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The file describes a 900-metre trail crossing the park, including a footbridge of about 150 metres, and assistance of up to $2,000,000 [CG26 0121].

The City approves construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform, then hands the project to the arrondissement de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The borough then awards a contract for $499,865.92, taxes included, to supply and install two greenhouses, with $74,979.88 in contingencies [CA26 14 0163].

The City awards a contract for $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, with $163,754.01 in contingencies. The work involves a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator and a controller to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223].

The borough awards a contract for a maximum of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, to redevelop rue De Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a total authorized expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings [CA26 14 0076].

The City awards two companies the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028. It also extends the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium by six months, for $193,215.49 more, taxes included [CG26 0521].

The City extends the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the complex by five months, for $296,349.21 more, taxes included; the compost is used in particular to landscape the park [CG26 0320]. In October, the borough authorizes the filing of a funding request to the Véloce III program for the bike lane and sidewalks on rue De Louvain Est.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is filing its application, ends on November 26, 2026.
Installation work on the greenhouses is due to finish in December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The extended snow removal contract covers November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs by unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, extra mortar, sod, and a deteriorated culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The application involves no spending; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are added to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité of the agglomeration, with conservation plans. The 2025 report submitted shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, representing 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

etapes.titre: Rebuilding of the chemin Senneville culvert
etapes.texte: A contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; the total expenditure reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow clearing, cleaning and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the contract for snow clearing of the service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors ($178,330.82, taxes included), and 9232-3914 Québec inc. the contract for the housekeeping of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other dying trees in the park, for a total expenditure of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow clearing of the service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Housekeeping of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and dying trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan to be submitted in February 2027, DarkSky International's response expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is setting up a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026 and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for the winter of 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for projects on inclusion, cohabitation in public space and awareness. The amounts cover a three-year period ending on December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and Bain St-Denis fit-out
etapes.texte: Council adopts a framework to receive private donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fit-out work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Rue Notre-Dame encampments and appeal proceedings
etapes.texte: The City awards a $149,520 contract, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to guide people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area towards shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the dispute over the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and projects for social, affordable or student housing, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: This year, the City approves the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the OMHM, transfers or purchases land for social housing, and pays grants to organizations building affordable housing. It also amends the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units [CM26 0114]. City council and the urban agglomeration council approve the 2026 budget of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households [CG26 0024].

The City accepts from the Government of Canada half the rights to a 3,658.8 square-metre plot of land on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost [CG26 0042]. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a 789.6 square-metre plot of land at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, where the co-op must build 26 housing units [CG26 0062].

The City adds $877,312 to its support for Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve [CG26 0171]. It grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project [CG26 0178].

etapes.titre: Land purchase and right of first refusal
etapes.texte: The City purchases, for $9,293,113 plus taxes, a vacant 1,535.1 square-metre plot of land near rue Chatham and rue William, in the Sud-Ouest, for social housing purposes [CG26 0286]. It withdraws the right of first refusal for social housing on lots in Ville-Marie and the Sud-Ouest that have been subject to it since 2020 [CG26 0292].

The City pays $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel for 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus [CG26 0372] and $13,151,528 to Immobilier collectif – Point commun for 395 units in Pointe-Saint-Charles [CG26 0559]. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build 72 housing units on 2e Avenue [CE26 1028], and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a policy reimbursing 50% of permit fees for eligible projects [CA26 170209].

aSurveiller.texte: Occupancy of the 350 housing units at the Technopôle Angus by April 30, 2027, at the latest.
Delivery of the SHDM's 72-unit building on 2e Avenue in May 2028.
Occupancy of the 395-unit building in Pointe-Saint-Charles in February 2030.
Integration of the fee exemption into the 2027 local fee by-law in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council extended the lease of a 2,787 square-metre lot to the Société de transport de Montréal, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, for a total rent of $49,293. It also extended the lease of a neighbouring 836 square-metre lot to an app-based parking company, for $45,049 before taxes.

City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités," because the first residential project is under construction and addresses need to be assigned. The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Contract for the street and the soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded Charex inc. the construction of a 610-metre street with sewer, water supply, lighting and underground electrical network, for $10,311,940.25 taxes included, and a total expenditure of $15,366,336. The contract includes the rehabilitation of the soil at the former gas station, for which the City is adding a net $2,007,312.15 from the environmental liability reserve.

The borough adopted a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a building complex, with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It then launched a draft by-law allowing, on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, a height limit of 73 metres and a floor area ratio of 6.

etapes.titre: Redevelopment of rue de Louvain Est
etapes.texte: The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 taxes included and a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. In October, it authorized the filing of a financial assistance application to the ministère des Transports for the bike lane and sidewalks of this section.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027; the Ville en vert vegetable garden is loaned until December 31, 2027.
Îlot 84 could occupy the Esplanade lot from April 1 to October 31, 2027.
Work on rue de Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks and curbs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
Four other public spaces in the eco-district remain to be named before the completion of the development, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, areas and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its contracts related to ecocentres, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the 2025 report on the agglomeration's residual materials management.

etapes.texte: The City is extending twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanize food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred at Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and Moose Creek, Ontario, while awaiting the commissioning of the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre.

etapes.titre: Purchase of bins and loan of sorting equipment
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to loan reusable dishes, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

The agglomeration is extending the contracts for garbage collection from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It is awarding Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from the ecocentres, assigning two firms studies on constructions located on former waste disposal sites, and extending the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program to loan dishes, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until no later than December 31, 2026.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The dumping authorization management software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former hippodrome Blue Bonnets: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former hippodrome Blue Bonnets, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It obtained an additional delay from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and public domain, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline extended to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Government of Québec grants the City a delay until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former hippodrome, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH that is used to pay for feasibility studies of the residential project. On the same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of public assets and funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City is borrowing $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil rehabilitation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, professional fees and land purchases. It is also borrowing $12,000,000 to build main waterworks pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and recreation centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and equipment in the sector.

The City is leasing parcels of the site to the community cafeteria MultiCaf and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transitional nursery. Each lease provides for a symbolic rent, and the organizations pay for development, upkeep and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Government of Québec to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The $128.3M federal subsidy is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031; the funds from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the transfer deed to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of the temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora and April 30, 2028 for the transitional nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.

etapes.titre: Plans and studies before the work
etapes.texte: The City is awarding the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of the parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil and environmental studies for the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for repairs to the heritage walls on the chemin de Senneville, is having a culvert rebuilt at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche, and is awarding contracts for snow removal and the felling of ash trees and dying trees. It is listing the Anse-à-l'Orme sector in the directory of protected natural environments and is submitting the Cap-Saint-Jacques bid for the Urban Night Sky Place designation.

The City and the boroughs are adding funds or shifting budgets for work already underway: oversight of the parc du Bassin-à-Bois, the parcs des Hirondelles and du Sault-au-Récollet, the parc Villeray, plans for the parc Percy-Walters, and the museography of the parc des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne in Lachine.

City council is removing a 810.2 m² stretch of street from the public domain to add it to the parc Campbell Ouest, in the Sud-Ouest. Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is requesting the same for a 75.2 m² strip of laneway that crosses the parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: City council must rule on October 19, 2026 on the removal of the laneway strip from the parc Le Prévost, after it goes before the executive committee on October 7, 2026.
For the artwork at the parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026 and installation in 2028.
The snow removal contract for the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Final acceptance of the work at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois is expected in June 2027, after the warranty year.
For the Cap-Saint-Jacques bid: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, and site compliance work in April 2032.
Work at the parc J.O.R.-Leduc, in LaSalle, must be completed by June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and regulating temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid out $2,694,500 to boroughs as part of the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the ordinances that close the streets and authorize terraces, sales and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a parcel of land, and an official name.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its business development corporations (sociétés de développement commercial) to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by ordinance [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee allocates $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the business development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

The borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre parcel of land at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from a street (public square) to a local park [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque « place Chez-Marguerite » [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The ordinance on sound ambiance for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The UPM and the conformity by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its conformity by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting six additional months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is reviewing its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing heights, uses and the building coverage ratio in the sector bordered by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on building demolition, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent's public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the deadline granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its conformity by-laws by June 16, 2027, a date set by the minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and to hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The Ville de Montréal's Service de police: contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: City council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to purchase and replace specialized public safety equipment for the SPVM between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a sergeant-detective to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City awards 9415-1966 Québec inc. the contract for meals for persons detained by the SPVM and extends by one year the computer-aided dispatch system software maintenance contract with Peraton International. It leases 50 parking spaces from the Société de la Place des arts, extends the lease of the training centre in Anjou and that of neighbourhood station 15 in Verdun, and accepts $8,000 from Ottawa for an information campaign on sexual assaults.

etapes.titre: Ammunition, courier services and building trades
etapes.texte: The City enters into an agreement with Agence Gravel for 9mm practice ammunition for firearms training, extends by one year the SPVM's courier contract, and renews the lease for neighbourhood station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings, and loans a sergeant-detective to the Sûreté du Québec team on the export of stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: On October 23, 2026: the Fraternité des policiers et policières's "Fèves au lard" day at neighbourhood station 46, for which the Anjou borough purchased 62 tickets.
On February 1, 2027: start of the 10-year lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.
On March 1, 2027: deadline for delivery of the harbour patrol boat and its trailer.
On March 31, 2027: end of the period covered by grants from the ACCES Tabac, ACCES Alcool, ACCES Cannabis and ACCEF committees.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the Société de transport de Montréal's (STM) 2026 budget and capital program, then a series of STM loan by-laws. It sells, leases or lends land to the STM for station entrances, ventilation plants and parking. It also oversees construction sites around the network and gives out mandates related to the extension of the blue line.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council tables then approves the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410 in both revenues and expenses, and its 2026-2035 capital program [CG26 0022]. The City also enters into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel [CG26 0064].

etapes.titre: Construction sites overseen around the network
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville modifies bus waiting posts as part of the network overhaul [CA26 09 0020], Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and redo the vault of the green line tunnel 24 hours a day from June 10 to July 31, 2026 [CA26 240269], and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks at bus stops [CA26 08 0373]. The City signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the Wiseman ventilation plant in Outremont [CM26 0198], does not object to the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel over the REM [CG26 0379] and adds $250,000 in related work to the Berri-UQAM station construction site, billable to the STM [CG26 0526].

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 [CG26 0175]. It then enters into framework agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée for the design and impact management of the blue line corridor redevelopment [CG26 0564], and city council adopts a motion asking Québec to study preserving the tunnel boring machine "Lisette" [CM26 0920].

The City purchases advertising space in the metro and buses for Espace pour la vie, up to $172,462.50 [CG26 0164], and pays $382,000 to the STM to strengthen service during the 2026 UCI Road World Championships [CG26 0461]. The borough councils of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle adopt motions calling for structuring public transit in the East and in the Grand Sud-Ouest.

The agglomeration approves several STM loans and the corresponding changes to the 2026-2035 capital program: analysis of MR-73 car replacement [CG26 0393], extension of their service life [CG26 0504], bus priority measures [CG26 0500], Réno-Infrastructures phase 4 increased to $640,000,000 [CG26 0501], surface infrastructure rehabilitation [CG26 0506] and technological and security risk management [CG26 0503].

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the Ahuntsic-Cartierville parking lot runs for three years starting October 1, 2026, for a maximum of 92 days per year.
The agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée cover 72 months, from October 2026 to October 2032.
The rehabilitation and expansion work on the Rielle ventilation plant, in Verdun, must continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel.
The opening of the five new stations from the blue line extension is planned for 2031.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-service bike system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI self-service bike system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new bike infrastructure projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an ordinance that officially establishes the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rues des Carrières and de Bellechasse and requires mandatory manoeuvres for drivers up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives to be spread, notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike lane work, including repairs to the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville hired Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleanup of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract worth $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then hired Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers used as a base for the stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal hired Cojalac inc. for work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and Le Sud-Ouest hired Groupe Damex inc. for the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial assistance from Québec
etapes.texte: City council authorized the submission of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to submit complete financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike lane on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
